data.validation_result: 43 of 44 lines pass in that log, and every --exact line prints `1 passed`. That covers the 33 Required-validation lines, including `cargo test -p sc-jev-check --lib -- payload::` added for REQ-SAG-0303, and all 11 workspace gates. The 44th line, `cargo publish --dry-run`, failed only because my private CARGO_HOME already held old copies of the 0.1.0 crates: cargo reuses an extracted crate with the same name and version, so it compiled pre-r-3 sc-jev-backends source that still uses ureq. With a brand-new empty CARGO_HOME it exits 0: /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-randlee--claude-spares-spare-ZVG33J/84ad1f90-7f83-4b6e-b4fc-63121d353959/scratchpad/r2-only/publish-f7994d5.log. That line now lists every published crate in order, including sc-agent-http from r-3; the sprint doc's own validation block predates r-3 and still lacks it. CI starts with a clean cache and passes.

per_id.note: A normal merge commit. docs/architecture.md and docs/requirements.md conflicted only where both sprints flipped markers on the same lines; I kept r-3's Active markers and r-2's Active markers on each line, plus r-2's REQ-SAG-0601 wording. cargo-tree-gates.sh, sc-agent-ci.yml and clippy.toml merged cleanly.

The ten missing ids are in the frontmatter `requirements`. The Implementation notes have a 'QA-1 requirement coverage' table with evidence for each. REQ-SAG-0703 is marked not applicable, because r-2 changes no install path.
ADR-SAG-0016 is in `adrs` with the upheld note, also stated in the notes: libraries take only SharedSessionLog, and sc-jev-check has no sc-observability edge.

equal_input, extract and payload are now pub(crate), as are build_payload, extract_input, load_check_str, parse_question_set, producer_from_extractions, the prompt-path types, SESSION_CONTEXT_HEADER, STALE_TMP_AGE and DEFAULT_SESSION_TTL. StoredSession and FileSessionStore::{save, load} are public only under test-util, and the session and sessions_exact targets now declare required-features = ["test-util"]. Tests that used the internals now go through prepare / run / ask or are --lib tests. The facade string lists every remaining public item. Sprint-doc section D2.9 and the deviation table record what stays public and why. No snapshot gate was added. The boundary check passes.

FileSessionStore no longer sends. Follow-ups go through run::ask(&FileSessionStore, SessionId, follow_up, RunConfig) -> AskResponse. run and ask now share one send step (judge, then one log event) and one function that builds the system prompt plus session context (session::contextual_prompt). This is recorded in the ADR-SAG-0024 FileSessionStore bullet.

CheckSource::CheckFile now holds a RepoRelativePath. CheckSource::check_file(&RepoRoot, &Path) is the one place a check path is normalised, and config::load_check_at takes &RepoRelativePath. The three hand-written normalisers are deleted: sc-ai relative_to_repo, sc-jev-py check_path_text, and the engine's check_path_text. The old sc-ai normalisation test moved into sc-jev-check.

tests/support/git_env.rs is the one shared GIT_* scrub. It uses the r-3c list including GIT_CONFIG_SYSTEM and GIT_DEFAULT_HASH, runs `init --object-format=sha1`, and disables hooks and signing. sc-jev-check's unit-test fixtures and tests/run_response.rs use it, as does sc-ai tests/cli.rs, all through spawn_with_deadline. No list is copy-pasted.

AskResponse carries outcome, session_id, prompt_sha256 and warnings, with with_warning. Envelope::ask(&AskResponse) writes them. sc-ai again reports an ask log-flush failure as a warning (CR-014), and ask data includes prompt_sha256 again; a cli test asserts it.
The Implementation notes cite the PR 27 CI job names and run ids at f7994d5, plus the validation log path.

discover_repo_root falls back to the start directory only when git is not installed, or when git finds no work tree and no ancestor holds `.git`. Everything else is INPUT_INVALID. The ADR-SAG-0003 r-2 text is narrowed to match, and a deterministic --lib test covers every branch.

I added the optional field as `producer = "..."` rather than the suggested `name`, because a `name` key would be confused with the input's table key. Without it the name falls back to the argv[0] stem. The REQ-SAG-0313 row records the interpreter case, and a test covers it.
The REQ-SAG-0710 amendment now reads `session_id` (null unless `session_saved`).

Envelope keeps the typed body and writes it only when serialized, so building it cannot panic. Keys come out in the documented order, pinned by run::tests::ask_envelope_carries_digest_warnings_and_readback_in_order. The pipe .expect calls now map to EXTRACTION_FAILED, and default_backends returns its error instead of unwrapping.

I chose to document rather than change behaviour. A failed session write stays fail-fast in r-2, and session_save_failed.json is a test_builder-only sample until r-2b. This is stated in the run module docs, the ADR-SAG-0024 landing bullet and the deviation table.
The tmp-name retry stops after 8 attempts. The parent-directory fsync after the rename is now best effort and documented in the concurrency model.

I split the case out, which FTQ-003 allows. A deterministic --lib test (classify_discovery) covers the outside-git branches, and I removed the machine-dependent branch from the integration test, with a comment saying so.
The re-executed env-probe child runs under spawn_with_deadline, and so do run_response's git fixtures.
Fixtures are rewritten only by the ignored test bless_run_response_samples, run by name with --ignored. The normal checks only compare.

The facade lists production items first, then the test-util group, with a manifest comment and notes saying so. sc_jev_check::run is now the only owner of the envelope constants; sc-ai's re-export is removed and its doc test and cli imports updated.
Optional, and the fix file says to leave it.
Ceremony-screened and already disclosed.
Informational.
Doc link fixed; rustdoc -D warnings passes locally and in CI run 42419966414.
